newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 9.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.
- Sinn Fein is unlikely to be at the multi-party talks when they resume on June 3.
- Tourist chiefs held a special meeting to discuss the negative reaction to the Irish Tourist Board's new logo and the attempt to change the country's image as a holiday destination.
- An overwhelming majority of voters believed Ben Dunne when he told a tribunal he had paid more than one million Irish pounds to former prime minister Charles Haughey.
- BUPA is to step up the health insurance war by offering consumers a new, cheaper package, directly targeting the most popular VHI plan.
- Aer Rianta, the Irish airports authority, has failed in its bid to become a part owner and manager of three of Australia's most profitable airports.

- A clear majority of voters - 65 percent - believe Ben Dunne's evidence to the Dunne Stores tribunal that he paid more than one million punts to former prime minister Charles Haughey, according to the latest Irish Times/MRBI poll.
- Fears of further pressure on the Irish pound have been alleviated by a sharp fall in the value of sterling.
- Government and opposition sources expect parliament to be dissolved next Thursday and a general election on June 6.

- Mo Mowlam will today launch the first of her confidence building measures in Northern Ireland with new public order rules requiring longer notice of parades and empowering police to confiscate alcohol from people attending marches.
- A clear signal that the IRA are serious about abandoning violence will be needed before a target date for Sinn Fein's inclusion in peace talks is set by the British government.
- A Donegal priest who was yesterday cleared of 19 charges of gross indecency involving altar boys, will return to his parish tomorrow to say Mass.
- Millions of pounds belonging to dead or discharged patients are being held by Ireland's eight health boards.
- Intense behind-the-scenes moves are taking place between Avonmore and Waterford Foods to see if they can agree merger terms.
